content.thinking:
Tracing the failure chain: account pages threw ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py once the monthly-spend-feature flag flipped on at 22:29, which started routing evaluations into the new code path.

I confirm the revert of that flag alone fixed things, and rule out the other feature flag since it switched on later, at 22:34, after onset had already begun. I also check deploys and rollout status — nothing new went out, and the rollout had already converged, so there's no deploy-related cause. The ClientDisconnected errors are pre-existing background noise starting before onset, so I rule those out too. Root cause: the spend summary function divides by this month's purchase count, which is zero for shoppers who bought previously but not in the current month — a straightforward logic flaw with no supporting log evidence needed.

There's no test coverage that catches shoppers with no purchases in the current month before this flag was enabled, so I'm thinking of contributing factors like a missing pre-enable check or a gradual rollout step, separate from whatever tests the fix PR adds.

Another factor is the flag jumped almost instantly from a small fraction (54/200) to fully on, with no staged rollout that halts on rising error rates — that's worth flagging as a fix. As for nobody being paged, Argus handled mitigation anyway so it probably wouldn't have changed the outcome, so I'm inclined to leave that out as a contributing factor rather than force it in.

Moving to action items: AI-3 would require flag rollouts on io-shop to happen in stages with automatic halt/revert if error rates climb, and AI-4 would add a pre-enable check.

AI-4's refinement is to run the flag's on-path tests against shoppers with prior purchases in CI before the flag can be switched on in production. I'm weighing whether to include AI-5 about paging on-call for HighErrorRate since nobody was actually paged — it's a bit of a stretch to tie to a specific factor, but I think it's reasonable to include as a detection improvement anyway.

For still_at_risk, I'll note that the division fault remains in the code with the flag off, so re-enabling monthly-spend-feature would likely cause the same failures again. For went_well, I'm capturing Argus reverting the flag after the alert and the investigator identifying the candidate fault, each tied to their timestamps, with nothing to note under went_wrong.

I'll leave got_lucky empty since the other flag toggle during the incident doesn't clearly qualify as luck. For assumptions, I'm noting that the theory about affected shoppers (prior purchases but none this month) comes from the code reading rather than verified data, and that the unrelated disconnect errors are likely background noise — avoiding specific line numbers or figures in the write-up.

Now I'm tracing the evidence chain: account page failures began with server error rates climbing to a worst-case peak (citing Gbac1, AL1, G5309), caused by ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary when a flag switch routed evaluations to the monthly path (P1, G971b, Gce95, T18, T21 confirm the revert). I want to build each step with precise citations and timestamps rather than vague wording.

Contributing factors worth noting: the flag rollout jumped from partial to full evaluation within a minute with no staged hold or automatic halt, which otherwise could have limited the blast radius. Also, there was no test exercising the monthly path for shoppers without this-month purchases, nor a pre-enable check running flag-on paths — pointing toward adding tests and a pre-flight check as action items.

action_items.item: Roll out io-shop feature flags in stages: hold each stage at a small share of traffic, and halt and revert the flag automatically when the error rate rises.
Require tests for code behind a feature flag to run with the flag on in CI before that flag can be switched on in production.

causal_chain.step: From {began}, account page requests failed for many shoppers. The share of requests answered with a server error rose from {errors_before} to an average of {errors_while_broken} while it was broken, and reached {errors_at_worst} at its worst.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, starting at {G5309.3}.

ruled_out.what: The feature flag an-unrelated-feature, which admin switched on at {P2.1}. That came after the onset at {began}, and the service recovered with this flag still on once only monthly-spend-feature was reverted.
A deploy or an unfinished rollout. No deploys came back when they were looked for, and all replicas were running one revision.
The ClientDisconnected account page errors. These were already being logged from {G46bc.3}, well before the onset, while account pages still rendered normally with the flag off.

causal_chain.step: Those requests reached the failing code because admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. By {G971b.1}, {G971b.3} of {G971b.4} flag evaluations came back on, and from {Gce95.4} every evaluation came back on. Turning the flag off again was judged CONFIRMED as the mitigation.

With the flag on, account pages compute the average spend per item this month. That calculation divides this month's spend by the number of this month's purchases, with nothing guarding against an empty count, so for shoppers who have bought before but not this month it raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.2}.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly-spending feature sent account pages through a calculation that crashed, likely for every shopper who had bought before but had bought nothing yet this month, because it tried to divide by that month's empty purchase count.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from a share of evaluations at {G971b.1} to all of them by {Gce95.4}. No staged rollout that holds at a small share, and no automatic halt when errors rose, was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have reached the failing path, and the rollout would have stopped itself once account page errors rose.

contributing_factors.factor: Before the flag was switched on in production, no test or check was seen that ran the monthly path for a shopper with past purchases but none this month. Code-Fix's reading says the existing test helper calls that shopper the ordinary case.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The failure would have been found before the flag reached any shopper.

went_well: The Investigator formed the leading candidate, C1, {T13.1 - T1.1} after Argus received the alert. The candidate pointed at the flag toggle and the exact failing line.
The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and judged the revert CONFIRMED {T21.1 - T18.1} after making it.
Argus left the unrelated flag, which was toggled during the incident, alone and reverted only the flag the evidence pointed to.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, account pages go through `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases they made this month, and nothing guards against that count being empty. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, it raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.2}, and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: The faulty calculation is likely still in the code with only the flag turned off, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix ships would again break account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
